content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file carefully in one pass since I can't test it, so I'm planning the biplane's proportions—roughly 7m long, 8m wingspan, 2.8m tall, facing +Z with wheels on the ground. I'm sketching out the fuselage approach, thinking through lofting sections along the z-axis to build the body shape.

Still designing the plane... fuselage via loft, cowling via lathe, propeller and spinner, upper/lower wings via extrude with rounded outlines, plus stripe and rib patterns painted onto the wing surfaces based on position.

Now I'm adding the struts and rigging between wings, two open cockpits with dark coaming rings, a whimsical pilot with goggles and a streaming scarf plus a little dog passenger, and finally landing gear with V-struts, wheels, and a tail fin and skid.

For decoration I'm thinking through pennants, exhaust pipes, a star roundel decal, the number "7" on the wings, and a "BARNSTORM" text banner across the fuselage using plane geometries oriented outward so the text reads correctly from both sides, plus a red-and-cream toon-shaded paint scheme for the body.

Now I'm working out geometry orientations: cylinders default to the y-axis so wheels need a dir along x, torus tires sit in the XY plane so they need dir [1,0,0] with axis "z", and I'm setting up a helper function for placing parts with color, position, and options. I'm also laying out the fuselage loft stations with their z-position, y-offset, width, and height to shape the body profile from nose to tail.

Continuing the cowling lathe outline, spinner cone, and cowl ring placement...

Now I'm positioning the wheels at z=0.7 with x±0.95, working out the gear strut rods connecting the fuselage to the axles, and figuring out the axle rod span and lower wing height.

Checking the tail skid bottom clearance and overall height, I'm now working out the fin geometry as an extruded outline positioned behind the fuselage, defining its points to taper from fuselage height to a small triangular tip.

Reworking the fin outline to make it more rounded at the trailing edge, and setting up a paint rule to add a white stripe near the front edge of the rudder.

Now moving to the stabilizer: extruding a rounded profile with wide span and shallow chord near the tail, then starting on the wing outline with rounded corner points spanning the full width.

For wing paint, I'm setting up a cream base color with red tips beyond a certain span, adding darker rib lines across the top face, and wrapping it in cel shading with normal-based lighting and a derived shadow.

I'm also adding wire bracing rods between strut tops and bottoms, and planning roundel decals on the fuselage sides using layered circle textures positioned based on the loft's cross-sectional width.

Now I'm shaping the propeller: two tapered blades extruded in the XY plane near the spinner, positioning them just ahead of the cowl with a thin outline that widens toward the tips, possibly rotated to suggest blade pitch.

I realize the bottom blade tip at -0.2 dips below the ground plane, so I'm shortening the blade half-length to about 1.1 to keep it clear, which also keeps the top within the upper wing's height. Now I'm checking the pilot/cockpit placement, with the rear cockpit around z -0.7 and the front cockpit near z 0.35 for the dog.

For the cockpit opening I'm adding a dark disc near the fuselage top around y 1.72 and a flat torus ring as the coaming lip, then placing a pilot figure with a sphere head and capsule-shaped torso in a brown leather jacket, topped with a partial-hemisphere leather helmet and cylindrical goggle rings with lenses.

I'm sketching a trailing scarf as a wavy curve from the neck and adding a dog riding along, built from a tan head sphere, snout capsule, flopping ear shapes, and a nose.

Now I'm working out the fuselage paint scheme -- layering a countershading function (red top fading to cream belly) inside a cel-shading wrapper, and adding yellow stripe bands at specific z-position ranges near the tail.

For detailing I'm adding exhaust pipe cylinders along the cowl, a ring of small rivet spheres around the cowl edge generated by looping sine/cosine positions and merging the geometries, and considering thin rod panel lines before deciding to stick with rivets instead.

Deciding to skip fuselage rivet rows and panel detailing in favor of simpler whimsical touches - maybe small pennant flags on the wingtip struts and a lantern, plus star-painted wheel hubs - while dropping ideas like bunting lines and cargo crates to keep things manageable before moving on to writing the actual code.

Setting up helper functions for boxes and wheels, working out the torus, cylinder, and hub geometry with proper orientation and sizing for the tire, hub, and axle components.

Now I'm figuring out the interplane struts connecting the lower and upper wings, computing the rod endpoints at front and rear positions based on the wing chord and vertical spacing between them.

I'm also adding outer struts further out along the span near x=3.4, plus cross wires between the inner and outer bays, and deciding to skip a center fuel tank since it'd clip into the upper wing.

Now I'm thinking about surface decoration: a roundel decal and a banner text ("WOBBLE & CO.") placed on the fuselage sides, positioning them so they don't overlap the cockpit opening, with another roundel on the tail fin and possibly a number plane on the wing top using a custom up-axis to avoid conflicting with the default orientation.

I'm also settling on the final color palette—reds, creams, yellows, teal, and browns for the plane and dog figure—and planning to add small black spheres for the dog's eyes before writing the full construction code.
